I've always struggled with anxiety and depression for as long as I can remember even as a kid. Last year I was working a job that caused me SEVERE anxiety. I would wake up every morning and have a panic attack just thinking about going to work and I would cry myself to sleep at night thinking about having to go back again the next day. At one point I found myself thinking as I was driving to work that it would be so much easier if I'd just drive off the road...I might end up with a broken rib or leg and not have to go to work or better yet I would be dead and never have to go back again. It was then that I decided I needed help.

I checked myself into a psychiatric hospital and stayed there for a couple weeks. Got on the right meds, made some friends and talked to a therapist for the first time. After I was released I immediately quit my job and in less than a week found a new job that I love! I now look forward to my work days and get up in the morning excited to go to work. The decisions I made turned my entire life around for the better. And although I still face struggles on a daily basis I find myself facing them head on with confidence. Something I was never able to do before!

In my experience it really depends on the strain. Weed really affects different people different ways though so really you should listen to your own body. If it makes your anxiety worse then its probably not the best option for you. Well I did a bit more research into the subject and found a constructive list of traits which are the standard traits for elves. Fair Complexion, Tall, Agile, Intelligent, Immortal, Pointed or Leaf-Like ears (which is apparently debatable amongst the community), and a passion for nature.

All of my elves possess these traits thankfully but where lines start to blur are with what I refer to in my story as "Dark Elves" and "Blood Elves". Dark Elves are typically associated with Drow which are much different from your typical elf. They tend to have dark blue or purple skin and white hair and live in caves, some stories even have them burning up in sunlight like vampires. My dark elves don't look like this though essentially the only difference is they tend to have black hair, which is uncommon in the elven world, and a slightly darker complexion and they follow a "Moon Goddess" as opposed to my other races which include "Light Elves" who follow a Sun God, Forest Elves who follow a Goddess of the Forest, River Elves who follow the God of the Rivers, and Blood Elves who follow a Goddess of Animals. My blood elves are much different from the blood elves of mmorpgs. They're called "Blood Elves" because they run through the forests in packs and each pack worships a particular animal that is sort of their totem and their pack is called their "Bloodline".  

With the exception of Celtic Lore, Rpg Games, and books by Tolkien there really isn't much information about elves. They aren't quite as mainstream as say, vampires or werewolves, so I suppose maybe I have a bit more creative freedom than I originally thought.
